params.body:
Forwarded mail now leaves the mail session with a triage rule, so every issue it opens carries a proposal the owner can accept or correct with a label change: a category, a priority, labels and a short summary.

## What changes

- `mail-triage.json`: the rule. A default (bug, request, question, feedback; P1 to P3) and per project slug what differs. The first project entry is `bextrust`: issues go to `abovebeyond-ai/bextrust`, categories landing-feedback (label `landing`), bug, question and request (`enhancement`), areas site, console, articles and brand, and three notes that keep issue text in line with how Bextrust is described (no "open source", ISBE not yet qualified, client copy stays verbatim).
- `lib/triage.mjs`: reads the rule, merges a project's entry over the default, builds the label set (`mail`, the category's labels, `priority:P<n>`, `area:<area>`) and the lines that go into the session's task.
- `mail-intake.mjs`: the task now includes those lines, and `hand.mjs issue` gets the triage labels instead of only `mail`. Each issue body opens with a **Triage proposal** block (category, priority, area, summary).
- README: the triage under *Forwarded mail*.

## Routing

Nothing new is needed on Portal's side: `bextrust@in.abovebeyond.ai` already resolves to the project through its slug (`Project::forMailbox`), and only owner mail that passes DMARC is kept. `PROJECTS.md` already maps `bextrust` to its checkout. The rule adds the repository, so a session no longer has to guess where a Bextrust issue belongs.

## Test notes

- `node --test lib/triage.test.mjs lib/policy.test.mjs`: 11 pass. The new tests cover the bextrust rule and the default fallback, the labels per category, priority and area, refusal of unknown values, and the lines that reach the task.
- `mail-intake.mjs --dry-run` with a stubbed mail for `bextrust` printed the full task with the triage section between the issue rule and the working rules (no herdr started, no state written).
- Not yet seen live: no Bextrust mail is waiting. After merge, forward one mail to bextrust@in.abovebeyond.ai and check that the issue has the triage block and the labels. `landing`, `feedback` and the `priority:*` / `area:*` labels do not exist in the repo yet; the issues API creates a missing label when it is set, the same way `mail` came to exist elsewhere. If the gateway's `issue.open` refuses unknown labels instead, create them once in the repo.
- The timer picks up the new code on its next run after projects-sync pulls `main`; nothing to restart.
params.title: Mail triage: category, priority, labels and summary on issues from forwarded mail
